chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), that he said:
There is no religion for one who obeys the created being in the disobedience of the Creator.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to have no religion according to Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* articulates a foundational Shia principle of *Tawhid* in governance and jurisprudence, asserting that religious validity is contingent upon the subordination of all created authority to divine command. It serves as a critical criterion for evaluating the legitimacy of leaders and scholars, ensuring that their obedience does not lead to *Ma'siyah* (disobedience) of Allah. This concept underscores the Shia view that true piety requires a hierarchical alignment where human decrees are valid only insofar as they do not contravene God's will.
